title: Hybrid signal-attn kernel with rotary-sparsity fusion and KV prefetch scheduler
author: Nikhil Rao
release_notes: Introduce a hybrid attention kernel (signal-attn) that fuses rotary sparsity paths and improves KV prefetch heuristics; ~12-18% end-to-end p99 latency reduction and 15-25% throughput uplift on common LLMs when using continuous batching.
description:
Motivation: Production workloads exhibit mixed sequence length distributions and intermittent sparsity from rotary/rope quantization artifacts. Existing Flash-style kernels are high-throughput for dense attention but underutilize opportunities where token locality and structured sparsity exist. This PR introduces 'signal-attn', a hybrid kernel that combines a fast-path Flash-like matmul for dense regions and a lightweight sparse-merge engine for rotary-sparsity lanes. The kernel integrates with the serving runtime scheduler using a signal-driven prefetch heuristic for the KV cache and a continuous-batching hint that reduces tail latency without sacrificing throughput.

Summary: Implement a new attention kernel and scheduler hooks that: 1) Detect per-batch rotary-sparsity patterns (simple entropy+mask heuristics) and route attention work to either dense or hybrid execution path. 2) Fuse rotary/rope application into the QKV projection pipeline to avoid an extra transpose+allocate in the hot path. 3) Add KV prefetch scheduler hints that prioritize hot shards and stagger prefetch to avoid PCIe contention under bursty arrival patterns. 4) Expose a runtime config flag to tune the hybrid threshold and continuous-batcher latency budget.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks run on p4d-like instance (A100 style) with representative models: - 7B dense: 15% throughput increase, 12% median latency reduction, 9% p99 reduction. - 13B mixed-length: 22% throughput increase, 17% median latency reduction, 18% p99 reduction. - 70B semi-sparse eval (synth rope sparsity): 25% throughput uplift on best-effort routing, 23% p99 reduction after warm-up. End-to-end synthetic RLHF workload saw a 14% token-cost reduction due to fewer recomputations and better batching. Full benchmark logs attached in artifacts.

Commits: single continuous-string summary of commits in this PR: "commit 1: core: add signal-attn kernel and hybrid exec path; commit 2: runtime: KV prefetch scheduler hints, continuous-batcher integration; commit 3: bindings: python and ts exposed config, tests and docs; commit 4: perf: microbench harness and regression tests; commit 5: fix: lint and CI fixes after review"

Changed files (high-level): "src/serve/attn/signal_attn_kernel.cpp", "include/serve/attn/signal_attn.h", "src/serve/attn/rotary_fuse.cpp", "src/serve/kernel_router.cpp", "src/serve/kv/prefetch_scheduler.cpp", "python/redwood/serve/attn.py", "ts/sdk/attnConfig.ts", "benchmarks/perf/signal_attn_harness.py", "tests/attn/test_signal_routing.cc", "docs/operational/attn_hybrid.md". Small API additions: config flag --attn.hybrid_threshold, --attn.kv_prefetch_window_ms.

Compatibility and safety: The hybrid path is opt-in by default and gated behind runtime config and per-model capability checks. Numeric stability tests (fp16/fp32) were added; all existing attention unit tests remain unchanged and pass. The kernel falls back to the dense Flash-compatible path if the mask/entropy heuristic is inconclusive or if quantized kernels are required.

Review notes: This PR intentionally keeps the rotor/rope fusion local to the attention hot path to avoid changing serialized model weights or checkpoints; only runtime transient transforms are applied. The rotary fuse uses aliasing-friendly in-place transforms to minimize extra allocations. The KV prefetcher introduces conservative heuristics first, with a progressive rollout via the continuous-batcher budget parameter to reduce the risk of PCIe saturation.

Operational impact: Rolling this out on Dedicated pools is recommended behind a canary policy (5% traffic) due to the scheduler prefetch behavior. Observability: added counters and histograms: attn.signal_route_{dense,hybrid}, attn.kv_prefetch_{issued,skipped}, attn.hybrid_fallback_reasons. These are surfaced in the console dashboards and can be used to tune hybrid_threshold and prefetch window.

Notes on tests: Added unit tests for routing heuristics and rotary fusion correctness, integration tests for continuous batching semantics, and perf harness scripts used for the measurements above.

perf_benchmarks: Detailed benchmark artifacts attached: artifacts/signal_attn/bench-20260301.tar.gz. Representative results: 7B dense (throughput +15%), 13B mixed (+22%), 70B semi-sparse (+25%). See bench harness for test harness parameters.
operational_recommendation: Canary 5% on Dedicated pools for 48 hours, monitor attn.signal_route_hybrid, attn.kv_prefetch_issued, and GPU PCIe stall metrics. If attn.hybrid_fallback_reasons > 5% revert hybrid_threshold down or disable feature flag.
notes: This PR aims to be conservative and opt-in; follow-up work will add adaptive hybrid_threshold tuning and more aggressive prefetch heuristics for enterprise customers.
